headline: Cancer models infer missing modalities and clone identity by linking molecular, imaging and clinical data
label: Cross Modal Cancer Inference
summary: Seven preprints link scRNA-seq, copy-number, histopathology and mutation data to assign clones, predict missing modalities and refine survival prognosis.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inferring information absent from one measurement by borrowing structure from another. KLONE assigns unpaired scRNA-seq cells to scDNA-seq copy-number clones through cross-modal Pearson similarity with balanced k-NN ensembles. OmniT2I converts molecular profiles to images, fuses them with histopathology embeddings through availability-aware fusion, and predicts missing modalities. EvoSurv adds a 38-dimensional evolutionary representation of mutation burden, spectra and copy-number change to clinical and RNA data for survival modeling. The SNOWS Bayesian network clusters gliomas on mutations, clinical variables and survival, raising C-index from 0.691 to 0.712 on CGGA transfer. scBoost, scDNM and the Geneformer clustering work concern cell-type classification and sit largely outside this thread.
